body: The HTTP cache is cleared only when `awaitDocument` found the navigated frame's 2xx Document response within its 1 s window. `awaitDocument` exists because Chromium can report the navigation error before the response event (technical.md, issue #186 section). The same spec also says 'A 2xx response that arrives after the error is also a failure'. In that case (`found == false`, the response comes late or is recorded under another frame id), the attachment body that the network stack already wrote to `<profile>/Default/Cache` is not cleared, and FR-AMZ-HCHK-014 ('no file from that response ... in the Amazon browser's persistent profile') is broken for that check. The tests cannot show this: the local fixture always delivers the response before the error. Suggested fix: clear the cache on every `errorText` path that does not return the error page, i.e. drop the `if found` guard (the clear stays best-effort and only logs). This fails closed and is simpler. The only cost is an extra cache clear after DNS or refused failures, which are already failed checks. Update the TS-AMZ-HCHK-017 bullet 'A navigation without a response ... unchanged' to match.

`downloadFile` ignores the `os.ReadFile` error, so a file it cannot read (permission denied, I/O error, a file still being written) passes as 'no download' even if it holds `DownloadMarker`. The helper is the evidence for FR-AMZ-HCHK-014 in TC-001 to TC-004, so it should fail closed. Suggested fix: return the error to the caller, e.g. make `downloadFile` return `(string, error)` and have the `WalkDir` callback return a non-`fs.ErrNotExist` read error, so `AssertNoDownload` reports it with `t.Fatalf` and does not silently skip the file.
